issue_context.title: Unclosed file on EmptyDataError
issue_context.body:
#### Code Sample, a copy-pastable example if possible

```python
import pandas
import psutil

proc = psutil.Process()
try:
    data = pandas.read_csv('kek.csv', engine='python')  # kek.csv is an empty file
except pandas.errors.EmptyDataError:
    pass

print(proc.open_files())

```
#### Problem description

Hi, there might be an unwanted behavior on attempt to read an empty `.csv` file, providing a
filename instead of handler, so it cannot be closed anymore by user on exception.

comments:
It appears that in the `__init__` method of `PythonParser`, the call to `_infer_columns` can raise exception `EmptyDataError`. 
This is not caught there and the file resource allocated in `get_handle` is never released here.
Simple fix is to put a try/except block around the `_infer_columns` call and to call `close()` to release all allocated file handles. But that leaves the rest of the `__init__` code unguarded for other exceptions. So should we put a very long try/except clause around the remaining code in `__init__` just to be sure?
So just put a try/except around `_infer_columns` or from the `self.handles.extend()` call after `get_handle` to the end of `__init__`?

We already have some machinery to wrap the function and check for a leak here:

https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/blob/25e2f8687f0a7033ddbbd6aa1b833d0586f99bad/pandas/util/_test_decorators.py#L236

Can you use this instead?

I tried it, but it doesn't trigger on this specific issue. Apparently the file handle gets destroyed by some other means before the check can trigger.
But I can double check.

I can choose between using the `tm.ensure_clean` context manager which will close the file as well and therefore prevent the file descriptor leak, or use the `check_file_leaks` context manager, but not both.
Please express a preference of one above the other.
I think should use the `check_file_leaks` context manager
OK, so that means I have to ditch the `tm.ensure_clean` call?
I'm not clear why they can't both be used together - what error were you getting?

Well, the `tm.ensure_clean` basically resolves the file descriptor leaked by `read_csv()`, so that the enclosing `check_file_leaks` does not trigger.
I always make sure that the test fails when I undo my change. And with both in place, the test succeeds even when the bug is present. Therefore the test becomes useless when both constructs are used in combination.

How are you setting that up? I see this as raising on master:

```python
with tm.ensure_clean() as path:
    def shouldnt_leak():
        try:
            pd.read_csv(path)
        except EmptyDataError:
            pass
        
    check_file_leaks(shouldnt_leak)()
```

Though admittedly intermittently
This seems to work for me, so it is now changed to use td.check_file_leaks in the right manner.

this should be

```
try: 
......
except EmptyDataError as err:
      self.close()
      raise from err
```
also I think ok to catch TypeError, ValueError, EmptyDataError here (all things raised by infer_columns)

The raise from clause only works in the case when you change the exception type, not in this case, so if you do `raise MyNewException from err`
`EmptyDataError` is derived from `ValueError` so I changed it to catch `ValueError` and `TypeError`
